sections.text: Horror was previously considered a niche genre, but internet culture, YouTube, and indie developers have driven it into the mainstream. sections.text: High street chemists in Britain report a rise in demand for the shingles vaccine, with bookings doubling at Boots and rising at Superdrug. sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: George A. Romero directed Season of the Witch, released in 1973 under the original title Hungry Wives. Marketed by the studio as softcore porn, the film failed to find an audience because it featured minimal nudity and focused heavily on dialogue. The distributor cut 40 minutes from the original 130-minute cut, though a later restoration expanded the released version to 104 minutes.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The film is a slow-burn feminist drama following protagonist Joan Mitchell as she escapes an abusive marriage through witchcraft. Despite low production values of $100,000 and uneven acting, the movie stands out for Romero's boldly progressive take on feminism and its tense, hallucinatory atmosphere.

Burnham argued that the public had not been sufficiently informed about foreign disruption. He warned that Russian disinformation is also affecting politics in Germany and France, and discussed the issue with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz.

sections.heading: What happens next

Burnham previously announced a new centre to counter disinformation, and his government will examine all options regarding the UK's future relationship with Brussels.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: English teacher and novelist John Branfield has died aged 95. Born in Somerset, he studied at Cambridge, taught in France and Middlesex, and later settled in Cornwall where he taught at Camborne County grammar school for girls until 1980. Alongside teaching, he wrote novels for adults and teenagers, later shifting to books about the Newlyn school of painters.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Branfield built a wider audience with teenage novels such as The Fox in Winter, which was runner-up for the Carnegie Medal for Writing. He and his late wife Pep also built an impressive collection of Cornish art and ceramics, which they loaned to local galleries and co-curated into exhibitions.

timeline.text: Indonesia looks to mosque loudspeakers to double as earthquake warning systems

gist: Indonesia is testing mosque loudspeakers to serve as earthquake early warning alarms.
A five-year joint research trial with Japanese scientists aims to reach remote communities.
Researchers are tailoring survival strategies to Indonesia's vulnerable, low-rise masonry buildings.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Scientists in earthquake-prone Indonesia have launched a pilot scheme linking mosque loudspeakers to a seismic sensor network. Conceived by Japanese disaster scientist Dr Inoue Hiroshi, the five-year project assesses whether speakers used for prayer calls can double as earthquake warning klaxons. Several mosques have already been hooked up to the system.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Indonesia has hundreds of thousands of mosques with well-maintained loudspeakers reaching remote areas where mobile infrastructure may fail during earthquakes. Because seismic waves travel rapidly, nearby communities might have only five to ten seconds to react. Additionally, unreinforced buildings in Indonesia mean international advice like "drop and cover" is often unsuitable, prompting tailored survival guidance.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Running until 2030, the prototype initiative aims to eventually issue public alerts. Researchers plan to test alarms via school loudspeakers, radio, and television, whilst conducting simulations and human experiments to develop science-based survival guidelines.

fivew: Researchers led by Dr Inoue Hiroshi and Andi Eka Sakya are conducting the project with the Indonesian government.

sections.text: Mike Love joined the Beach Boys on stage at PNC Pavilion in Cincinnati, Ohio, for their first public show since July. The 85-year-old co-founder, who is experiencing serious health challenges, was helped on stage by his son Christian Love and John Stamos. Love remained seated throughout the performance, singing back-up vocals and thanking attendees.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Love insisted on performing despite doctors, family and friends urging him to concentrate on his health. Band member Stamos explained that Love needs the stage, audience and fellow musicians to lift him up, following recoveries from bronchitis and Covid, alongside personal grief.

sections.heading: What happens next

stories.title: Is it true that … muscle turns into fat if you stop working out?

articles.title: Is it true that … muscle turns into fat if you stop working out?
articles.standfirst: If you take a break from the gym you may lose muscle and gain fat, but it isn’t as simple as one turning into the other

timeline.text: Is it true that … muscle turns into fat if you stop working out?

gist: Muscle and fat are completely distinct tissues and muscle cannot turn into fat.
Stopping exercise can cause muscle loss and fat gain, creating a false impression.
Dietary changes and maintaining consistent exercise habits over time help manage these fluctuations.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: People taking breaks from exercise often worry that their muscle has turned into fat or softened.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: There is no biochemical process linking muscle and fat. The perception of transformation arises from simultaneous muscle loss and fat gain caused by reduced activity and potential energy surpluses.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Experts recommend keeping protein intake high and slightly reducing calorie intake during breaks. Small fluctuations are normal as long as consistent exercise and dietary habits are maintained over months and years.

fivew: Experts explain whether muscle can turn into fat when someone stops working out.
To clarify the common misconception that muscle tissue converts directly into fat.

gist: Ecologist Daisy Dent studies natural rainforest regeneration in Panama.
Natural forest regrowth often outperforms expensive monoculture tree-planting schemes.
Supporting animal and plant interactions is key to restoring resilient ecosystems.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Forest ecologist Daisy Dent has spent decades studying unplanted secondary forests across the Barro Colorado Nature Monument in Panama, tracking how waves of tree life rise from bare earth.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Research shows that naturally regenerated secondary forests can capture carbon effectively and build resilient ecosystems, proving that large monocrop planting programs can be expensive mistakes.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Dent and collaborators are working with nonprofits and carbon-crediting startups like Ponterra to determine when ecosystems can regenerate independently and when they need human intervention.

gist: Sinn Fein ministers face a no-confidence vote following a dispute over Drumcree.
The DUP experiences internal divisions regarding how to respond to the situation.
DUP leaders state they will not collapse the Stormont government.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Sinn Fein ministers face a no-confidence vote following a dispute concerning Drumcree. Some members of the DUP called for the removal of the deputy first minister to trigger the removal of the first minister, while other party figures stated that government operations cannot continue as normal. However, DUP leadership noted that the no-confidence vote cannot succeed due to the existing governmental system and confirmed the party will not collapse Stormont.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The dispute highlights tensions within the four-party devolved government, particularly regarding how ministers should respond when individuals break the law, prompting debates within the DUP on the appropriate level of political action.

Outlets disagree slightly on settlement availability, and future updates depend on player numbers.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Hello Games announced that No Man’s Sky is launching on the iPhone and iPad, playable from the iPhone 11 and third-generation iPad Air upwards. It includes past updates and features redesigned touch controls. While Ars Technica states settlements run on the iPhone 15 Pro and later, The Verge describes planetary settlements as entirely missing.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The release brings the expansive procedural galaxy to mobile hardware with a 5GB download. Aside from missing multiplayer, it offers nearly the complete experience after a decade of transformative updates.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The game arrives on 28 October and will be free to try. Future support and content updates will depend on player feedback and active numbers.

gist: Stellantis and Renault want the UK included in upcoming EU protection rules.
Executives suggested the British government should think about limiting Chinese car imports.
The EU plans to restrict certain vehicle imports from China to protect local manufacturing.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Stellantis and Renault bosses supported including the UK in proposed EU measures meant to shield local vehicle production. Speaking in Paris, they argued that Britain ought to be treated like an EU member state under the upcoming Industrial Accelerator Act, provided the UK addresses concerns regarding Chinese vehicle imports.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: European automotive makers face intense pressure from lower demand and soaring Chinese market share. Including the UK could safeguard cross-border manufacturing footprints, but disagreements remain over whether Britain should restrict Chinese imports similarly to the EU.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The EU intends to enforce a quota on Chinese hybrid vehicle imports starting in December. Meanwhile, the UK government is reviewing its stance on whether to impose its own tariffs on Chinese vehicle imports.

gist: Chip shares fell globally following comments by Broadcom boss Hock Tan.
Tan likened some artificial intelligence investors to casino gamblers without understanding.
Reports of progress by Chinese memory chip maker CXMT added to market worries.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Semiconductor shares fell on Tuesday after Broadcom boss Hock Tan compared artificial intelligence investors to casino gamblers. Asian markets tumbled, including South Korea's benchmark Kospi index down 6.25%, alongside drops in Japan and Taiwan. US stock futures pointed to a mixed open after Nasdaq slipped previously. Markets also reacted to reports that Chinese memory chip maker CXMT made progress on a new architecture.

sections.heading: Why it matters

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Researchers created a computer-generated rendition of a rufous-collared sparrow song from the 1960s that had disappeared from a Buenos Aires park. Less than three months after playing it, a local bird began to copy parts of the tune. In another project, translocated cirl buntings initially produced abnormal songs before returning to normal over several years.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Birdsong is an essential part of animal culture and population health. Birds that sing well in a familiar dialect are better placed to find mates, defend territory and survive. Population declines and human encroachment can cause songs to change or disappear, threatening breeding success.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Scientists hope synthetic recordings and AI could help teach birdsong to dwindling or endangered species where real-life recordings do not exist. Researchers continue to register dialects and communication systematically.

gist: Celtic beat Motherwell 2-0 to return to the Scottish Premiership summit.
Winger Jota returned from injury after 18 months on the sidelines.
The victory helped lift recent gloom following three straight defeats.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Martin O'Neill's Celtic side returned to winning ways by beating Motherwell 2-0 away at Fir Park. Camilo Duran opened the scoring early on and Benjamin Nygren secured the victory in the second half. Winger Jota also made his long-awaited return from injury as a 74th-minute substitute after nearly 18 months out.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The win provided welcome cheer for disgruntled fans after three straight defeats, including two losses against rivals Rangers. It returned Celtic to the Scottish Premiership summit and eased recent pressure on manager Martin O'Neill.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Following the victory, Celtic will now turn their focus to upcoming fixtures, with Martin O'Neill noting after the match to see what Thursday brings.

To respond to a recent run of three straight defeats and lift club gloom.

sections.text: Manchester City faced charges related to inflating sponsorship income and expenses between 2009 and 2018. BBC Sport calculated that thirty-five other top-flight clubs were left financially out of pocket due to missed prize money, relegation costs, and missed European qualification.

Australia reached 33 without loss to lead South Africa by 139 runs.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: On day three in Durban, Australia dismissed South Africa for 284. Pat Cummins took three wickets, whilst Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon claimed two each. Steve Smith took three catches, including two off reverse sweeps. Australia finished the day on 33 without loss, holding a 139-run lead.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Australia's bowling quartet reached 607 combined Test wickets, countering concerns about the ageing side. Smith took his career tally to 223 catches, moving ahead of Joe Root for the most Test catches taken by a non-wicketkeeper.

This event marks Africa's return to the F1 calendar for the first time since 1993.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Rwanda signed a 10-year agreement with Formula 1 to host a grand prix in the early 2030s. A new circuit will be built in Bugesera, near Kigali.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: It is the first Formula 1 race in Africa since 1993, allowing the sport to race on every inhabited continent.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Construction will involve track architects, and the exact calendar placement will be determined to avoid main rain seasons.

fivew: Rwanda signed a 10-year deal to host Formula 1 races.
To bring the sport back to Africa and expand its profile.

quotes.text: For more than three decades, the world's premier motorsport championship has raced without this continent, and that changes with this agreement.
Africa has always been part of Formula 1's future, and from the beginning we were determined to return in the right way

gist: The DP World Tour will block LIV Golf participants from its 2027 membership.
Players face choices regarding tour participation as the European circuit adopts stricter regulations.
The policy change coincides with ongoing alliance negotiations involving the PGA Tour.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The DP World Tour announced that golfers joining LIV Golf next year cannot hold membership on the European circuit by 2027. Tour executives stated that competitors must choose their circuit rather than combining tours.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The decision marks a much tougher approach compared to previous seasons when conditional releases allowed participation in both circuits. Officials noted that LIV offering players equity conflicts with the European tour operating as a members organisation.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Competitors face registration deadlines in the coming weeks to determine their circuit intentions for the upcoming season.

fivew: The DP World Tour and professional golfers.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: San Francisco defeated Seattle 32-29 in a brutal divisional contest. The Minnesota Vikings beat the New Orleans Saints 23-13. The Baltimore Ravens beat the Atlanta Falcons 30-23 in overtime, and the New York Jets defeated the Cleveland Browns 17-12.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: San Francisco and Minnesota both reached 5-0 records, placing them among the standout teams of the early season. The 49ers showed their potential Super Bowl capabilities, while defensive masterclasses shaped several results across the league.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Arsenal came from behind to beat Leeds 2-1 at Emirates Stadium. After falling behind in the 55th minute, Riccardo Calafiori equalised before substitute Bruno Guimaraes scored the winner. Defender Piero Hincapie was later carried off with an injury during the warm-down.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The victory moves Mikel Arteta's side level on points with league leaders Manchester City. However, defensive frailties and attacking struggles continue to raise concerns about their title defence.

sections.heading: What happens next

gist: Andy Burnham will release details of his meetings with Manchester City.

Some Premier League clubs expressed concern over potential political interference.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated he will publish details of his past meetings with senior figures at Manchester City. The announcement follows criticism of his previous remarks after an independent commission found Manchester City guilty of financial rule breaches. Manchester City deny wrongdoing and have lodged an appeal.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Burnham's previous role as mayor and his relationship with the club's ownership raised questions from the opposition and Premier League clubs, who voiced concerns about political interference while sanctions and appeals are pending.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Manchester City played their first game since being found guilty of one hundred and fourteen charges relating to Premier League financial rules. Despite a hostile reception at Anfield, City secured a three to zero victory over Liverpool with second-half goals from Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The win occurred while Manchester City await potential sanctions, leaving the Premier League season in a holding pattern of uncertainty. Every victory now carries questions and a metaphorical asterisk until final decisions are made.

fivew: Manchester City defeated Liverpool three to zero.
Manchester City played their first match since being found guilty of financial rule breaches.

quotes.text: We knew there was going to be noise but we need to make our own noise by winning games.
For every single person part of Manchester City, every fan, this is a lovely moment that will stay with us for a long time.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Manchester United conceded an injury-time equaliser against a Tottenham side reduced to 10 men following Rodrigo Bentancur's red card. Dominic Solanke scored past goalkeeper Senne Lammens after Lisandro Martinez was outmuscled, leading to boos from fans at the end of the match.

sections.text: Manager Michael Carrick is under severe pressure as belief begins to ebb away. Pundits noted that opponents consistently outrun United, and the team is struggling defensively in key moments, failing to secure necessary points.

gist: Celtic beat Motherwell 2-0 to return to the Scottish Premiership summit.
Winger Jota made his long-awaited return from injury after 18 months.
The victory helped lift recent gloom following three straight defeats.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Celtic returned to winning ways by beating Motherwell 2-0 at Fir Park, with goals from Camilo Duran and Benjamin Nygren. The victory moved Martin O'Neill's side back to the Scottish Premiership summit following three straight defeats. Winger Jota also made his long-awaited return from injury as a substitute after almost 18 months on the sidelines.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The win provided welcome cheer for a disgruntled fanbase and lifted the recent gloom surrounding the club. It eases the pressure on manager Martin O'Neill, who had previously questioned whether he had the energy to continue following defeats against Rangers.

fivew: Celtic beat Motherwell 2-0 and returned to the Scottish Premiership summit.
To bounce back from three straight defeats and lift recent club gloom.

quotes.text: I was waiting on this for a long time
Of course, there was a lot of noise and a lot of it we brought on ourselves as well too.
